sections.owner_decisions:
Binding owner decisions — verbatim

The complete decision input follows verbatim. It takes precedence over research recommendations and superseded invariants; changes to those invariants are explicitly identified below.

```text
# Owner decisions 2026-10-18 (binding) — hackathons, event roles, uploads, yuyu gaps, pages

Earlier answers: certificates get a public verification page (QR + certificate ID → event, date, valid/revoked only);
event badges/ID cards carry a QR that works as the EVENT CHECK-IN TICKET and identifies the MEMBER; hackathon teams:
ALL types supported, organizer chooses per hackathon (solo, individual-apply-then-team, team-applies-together, team
finder); submissions take BOTH uploads and links, including hardware (PCB, CAD, firmware); ALL maker file formats must
be supported AND tested; Mentor Desk (github.com/jasimcm/mentor-desk, MIT) features included; organizers/co-organizers
can be selected; volunteer role with "volunteers needed"; mentor assignment; organization page shows its makerspaces +
its events across its own and other makerspaces; everything inside Events and in the Space Works brand.

Owner reply to the 27-item list: "all recommended" EXCEPT #3 — NO age limit (no minimum-age setting, no minors /
guardian-consent features). Plus: adopt yuyu's new and fun elements incl. easter eggs, re-done in our brand guidelines.

1 Hackathons = opt-in feature inside Events per makerspace, off by default.
2 Application: auto / rolling / batch (organizer picks), staged private decisions + bulk notify, RSVP deadline (default
  4 days), waitlist + overbooking.
3 (DROPPED) no age limit / minors features.
4 Travel reimbursement: not now.
5 Review: N reviewers per application, anchored rubric, optional blind mode.
6 Judging: weighted 1–5 rubric or top-3 stack ranking; pairwise later.
7 Public project gallery: organizer publishes once; only items teams mark public.
8 Integrity: AI-use declaration; optional GitHub "first commit before kickoff" FLAG only (never auto-disqualify).
9 Code-of-conduct consent required per hackathon; MLH data-sharing fields optional.
10 Mentor Desk: help queue core; optional mentor check-in rounds (locks, fresh eyes, conflicts) + mentor analytics.
11 Help requests raised by teams themselves and by mentors; alerts to on-shift mentors via chat platforms + in-app.
12 Mentor ↔ team assignment: manual, round-robin, skill-based.
13 Sponsor reps: own track's submissions; résumés only with explicit participant opt-in.
14 Volunteers: "needed" listings, shifts with capacity/waitlist, approval, shift check-in/out, hours, thank-you certificate.
15 Co-organizers may invite volunteers/mentors/judges with only the permissions they hold.
16 Virus scanning: optional ClamAV service (off in dev, recommended in production).
17 Video: ffprobe duration/resolution checks; no transcoding yet; judges play originals.
18 Storage: per-event budget; self-host unlimited; managed SaaS hackathon tier 25 GB per hackathon event.
19 Previews: 3D (STL/OBJ/3MF; STEP/IGES on click) + Gerber now; KiCad viewer later.
20 Retention: delete submission files 365 days after results, keep records + hashes.
21 Build ALL 15 yuyu gaps (layered certificate builder; bulk issue + template library; desk ID-card printing; form
   builder v2 with show-if; broadcast composer v2; readiness checklist; event-day mode; analytics funnel; live ticket;
   short links; cover photo editor; publishing three questions + unsaved-changes bar; accent presets; leave
   organisation + security activity + series guest list; platform insights).
22 Event accent: brand-palette presets only.
23 Shared handle namespace (members, makerspaces, organizations); existing member handles win; default handle = slug.
24 Published page of a superadmin-access-off makerspace stays public, not in the directory.
25 Team section links only to public member profiles; staff private data never shown.
26 Superadmin cannot reset Space Managers while access is off (keep as built).
27 Chat PDFs on by default — verify, fix if not, with a test.

## Owner addition (later 2026-10-18, binding)
28 Registration autofill: when a member registers (events, hackathon applications, volunteer/mentor applications), the
   personal data they enter is saved to their own member account and pre-fills every later registration form — e.g.
   name, phone, school/college/organisation, level of study, country, skills, links (GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio),
   résumé file, t-shirt size, dietary needs, accessibility needs, emergency contact. Requirements: a per-field "save to my
   profile" choice (default on, unticked for sensitive fields such as dietary/accessibility/emergency contact unless the
   member opts in), a "Saved details" page in the member account to view/edit/delete each item, saved data never shown
   to organizers except as the answers actually submitted to their event, encrypted where the scoped PII encryption
   rules require, included in data export and deleted with the account; mapping from event form questions to saved
   profile fields via a well-known field key (custom questions can opt in to a standard key).
29 "Make sure all things are built": nothing in this programme may be deferred silently — any item a lane cannot finish
   must be reported and scheduled into a follow-up lane before integration.
30 Date of birth + automatic age: the saved member details include date of birth (sensitive: encrypted under the scoped
   PII encryption rules, opt-in to save, editable/deletable on the Saved details page, in data export, deleted with the
   account). Age is NEVER stored — it is computed from DOB whenever needed, so it advances automatically every year; an
   event/hackathon form question "age" is answered with the age AS OF THE EVENT START DATE (and recomputed if the event
   date changes before submission is locked); organizers see the computed age only, unless their form explicitly asks
   for date of birth (then the member sees that before submitting). Still NO age limit / minors gating (decision 3).
31 Theme: EVERYTHING in this programme (hackathons, roles, pages, yuyu gaps, delight pack, easter eggs, autofill) is built
   ONLY in the Space Works theme — docs/brand guidelines, our CSS-variable tokens (light + dark), Gilroy 400–700 with one
   Unbounded accent per layout, lucide-react icons, components/layouts inside the AppShell, existing UI primitives,
   accessibility floor + colour vocabulary. No yuyu (or other product) look, fonts, palettes, illustrations or copy; any
   new illustration/glyph is an original Space Works asset. Frontend review checks this explicitly (Impeccable audit).
32 Artwork: every illustration/glyph the programme needs is produced as ORIGINAL Space Works artwork (SVG, light + dark
   variants, built from docs/brand symbol/lockups, brand tokens and the guidelines PDF; no third-party or yuyu assets):
   mood glyph set (welcome, success, waiting, empty, error), brand loader, 404 perforated equipment tag, optional maker-
   robot companion, empty-state illustrations per area, landing demo illustrations (light/dark twins), hackathon /
   volunteer / mentor / judge illustrations, default certificate templates (2–3, using merge tags + logo layer) and
   default badge/ID-card templates (Classic / Bold / Minimal, with member photo + logo + QR), live pass/ticket art. A
   dedicated artwork lane owns frontend/src/assets/illustrations/** (+ backend default template seeds) with an
   accessibility check (decorative = aria-hidden, meaningful = alt text) and a visual review.
33 Member profile photo already exists (makerspaces/models_profiles.py avatar_key + profile_images.py + member account
   upload) — reuse it for badges/ID cards, team cards and mentor/judge cards; staff accounts have no profile by design.
```
sections.authority_and_locks:
Feature gates, authority and common transaction contract

### Feature declarations

Add `makerspaces/capability_definitions_events_programme.py`, registered by the existing capability catalogue. No new module key. All conjunctions include deployment edition/runtime, tenant servability and installed `events`:

| Capability | Parent/default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `events.hackathons` | Events, **off** | Application/team/project/judging APIs and hackathon configuration. Event additionally has a `HackathonConfig` row explicitly enabled by an event manager. |
| `events.mentoring` | `events.hackathons`, off | Help queue, mentor assignment and office hours. |
| `events.mentor_rounds` | `events.mentoring`, off | Check-in rounds, locks, nominations and round analytics. |
| `events.volunteering` | Events, off | Needed postings, shift signup/attendance/hours. General event contributions and existing grants remain usable without this feature. |
| `events.project_gallery` | `events.hackathons`, off | Explicit publication and public project reads; embedded website sections additionally require website release. |

Use existing certificate/designer, badges, feedback, analytics, broadcasts/email/notifications and offline-check-in gates where available; enumerate the real catalogue rather than inventing parallel switches. Certificate verification is controlled by issuance publication consent, not a second paid module. New enhanced components are available under their existing domain feature. Disablement blocks new actions/delivery but preserves records and private history under the established history rules; explicit expiry/purge remains possible through lifecycle-owned services. Retention registration survives Events tombstoning. Event clone copies configuration, rubric/forms and templates with new owned keys but no people, applications, teams, scores, credentials, grants, results or publication pointers.

### Authority matrix

Continue to use `event_authority.can/require/events_for`; never widen tenant RBAC or `scope_by_makerspace` from a grant. The actor's account kind, standing, host, module, source gate and live authority are checked at both view and locked service boundaries.

| Operation | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| Event configuration, deletion/collaboration, money, results/gallery finalization, certificate issue/revoke/bulk, scoped PII reports | Existing full event manager (`permission=None`), with existing extra report/reauth requirements. Co-organizer grant alone is insufficient. |
| Application review/staging/offer release/RSVP override | New `review_applications` permission; roster/contact exports still need `manage_registrations` **and** tenant `VIEW_AUDIT`. Review does not grant money access. |
| Team moderation, submission triage/amend with reason | New `manage_hackathon` permission; no automatic grant of private form/contact answers. |
| Invite volunteer/mentor/judge helpers | New `manage_team`, requested permission subset of inviter's live delegable permissions, bounded event/track/time scope. |
| Help queue and assigned rounds | New `mentor_queue`; own role approved, on-shift, proper assignment/skill/conflict checks. |
| Score/review projects | New `judge`, plus an active assignment to this round and frozen submission. |
| Application reviewer | `review_applications` plus review assignment; blind-mode projection enforced server-side. |
| Sponsor submission access | New `view_sponsor_track` plus active rep assignment to exact sponsor tracks; no generic roster or other tracks, scores, reviewer notes or resumes. |
| Shift management and verified hours | New `manage_volunteers`; self signup/check-in/out uses owner action, not tenant authority. |
| Check-in/print/live ticket | Existing `check_in` for desk actions; participant owner for their ticket. Badge design editing cannot grant printing privileges. |
| Website/design/form/broadcast actions | Existing exact field permissions and new explicit form/broadcast service predicates; never authorize by a display role label. Preserve full-manager-only actions above. |

Co-organizer preset contains the existing event editing/registration/invitation/check-in/schedule permissions plus explicit review, hackathon, volunteer and helper permissions selected by a full manager. It may include mentor/judge/sponsor delegable permissions so it can invite those roles. Holding `judge` never bypasses assignment or conflict checks. The preset excludes full management, delete, collaboration, money, certificate issue/revoke and final publication. `manage_team` itself is not delegable by a co-organizer; only full managers appoint co-organizers. Co-organizers cannot edit/revoke grants whose permissions or scope they do not themselves hold.

Keep `can_manage_grants`' full-manager meaning because existing callers use it as full authority. Add `can_delegate_helpers(actor,target,permissions,scope)` and a distinct adapter admission predicate for helper invitations; do not change `can(...,None)` to include co-organizers. Extend shared grant lifecycle with an optional operation-aware subset/scope validator, defaulting to existing behavior for Bookings. Recheck inviter authority at **redemption**, including track, validity interval and allowed helper roles. Require current server-owned reauthentication for grant management; invitation redemption uses authenticated verified identity as already designed.

### Transactions, source gates and state ownership

- Every state machine has exactly one workflow entry module specified in later sections. Views, tasks, imports, `/control/` actions and frontend commands call it. Cross-domain actions call the owning service; no direct status updates from consumers or signals. DB checks/partial uniqueness protect illegal shapes; DB triggers protect frozen snapshots and append-only records.
- Common lock order: source-gate boundary on its existing lock-only connection; **PII global shared mapped-write fence, then affected tenant fences in ascending tenant ID, then affected account fences in ascending account ID**; series/event resources in their shipped order (events sorted for a multi-event command); host and collaboration/payment makerspaces sorted by ID; `lock_authority` membership/grant rows; ticket/config/capacity parents; domain parents then children sorted by PK. Invoke `assert_mapped_write_allowed(host_id)` before `_locked_event`, as shipped registration does; the DB trigger is a backstop, not the first fence acquisition after an event lock. G supplies a combined fence helper that acquires global once and all declared scopes in this order; no downstream mapper lazily expands the scope set. Account-only writes take global→account fences and never an unrelated tenant fence. Team, cohort, shift, office-hour slot and mentor claim operations lock their parent before children. Never combine nullable `select_related()` with `select_for_update()` or reacquire an earlier lock class downstream. Provide internal already-locked service methods with asserted lock context.
- All capacity calculations happen while holding the event/config/ticket or shift parent `select_for_update()` lock, using authoritative committed rows rather than UI counts. Lowering a capacity below existing allocations is refused unless an explicit overbooking change records the new ceiling; never silently evict people.
- Source migration uses the existing lock-only connection boundary, not a whole-request application `atomic()`. Register HTTP, task, direct service, scanner, upload-completion, cleanup and fan-out paths; task source-gate refusal retries safely. External storage, scanner/ffprobe, chat and email I/O happen outside application row-lock transactions using persisted claims, then fenced finalization.
- Audit via `audit.services.record`: actor, action, target, old/new enums, reason code, safe IDs/counts/revision. Text reasons/notes that may contain PII live in encrypted domain records; audits reference them. No contact details, answers, score comments, help text, credentials, signed URLs, PDF bytes or request IDs in audit metadata.
- Each mutable aggregate has integer `version`; commands check `expected_version`. Stable operation UUIDs and DB uniqueness make retries idempotent. Notification intent and work-item rows commit with state; enqueue on commit plus periodic sweeper recovers loss. Tasks use bounded claims, leases and attempt counters, not long DB transactions around I/O.

The PII maintenance fence and tenant source-migration gate are separate controls; passing either is not passing both. Use `423 pii_write_fenced` for a known authorized mapped write under maintenance, `423 source_frozen` for migration, with no domain mutation. A fence retry restarts the entire command before row locks. Discover target tenant/account IDs by nonlocking reads, then revalidate ownership under locks; if the required set changes, roll back and restart rather than extend it out of order. Event update/date-revision hooks also take the mapped-write fence before event locks because they affect answer derivation state. Cancellation, cleanup, import and task paths obey the same order; an erasure/maintenance worker uses only its explicit fenced-operation capability.

Account keys and `SavedDetailUpdateIntent` require a separate **preparation phase** (§10A): outside the event transaction prepare the owner key/encryption context and encrypted bounded candidate payload, performing broker/KMS I/O there. Under event locks insert only an already encrypted, validated intent; never call first-use key provisioning, lock `User`/`AccountPiiKey`, or unwrap via KMS from an event service. Account row locks belong only to later account-only transactions. Revocation/erase/rotation services take the account fence exclusively before key/account rows; event intent insertion holds the matching shared account fence and validates the prepared key epoch without locking those rows. This closes the prepare→commit erasure race without event↔account inversion.
sections.http_and_services:
Shared HTTP and service contracts — freeze before lane work

The integrator publishes canonical fixture objects and the following contract checkpoint before parallel implementation. Each lane owns its package's serializers, views, URL module and examples; the integrator alone mounts common URL barrels and regenerates schema/client snapshots. No lane invents a different response casing or permission model. Use integer DB IDs for authenticated resources, UUIDs only for public opaque identities. All datetimes are ISO-8601 UTC plus event timezone; bytes/minutes are integers and monetary values remain the existing decimal/currency types.

Common list response: `{count,next,previous,results}`, page size 24. Common aggregate response contains `id,event_id,version,allowed_actions` and typed domain fields; authority flags are explanatory only. PATCH sends only edited fields. Domain POST commands include `operation_id` UUID and `expected_version`; creates/uploads use `Idempotency-Key`, bound to actor+event+method+path+normalized body digest. Persist bounded `EventCommandReceipt(event,actor,operation_uuid,request_sha256,response_reference,created_at)` for command retries (credential responses never persisted). Unique event/actor/operation; different digest gives `idempotency_conflict`. Accounts uses P's separate owner-scoped `SavedDetailCommandReceipt` with the same digest/replay protocol and no fake Event FK or import of Events. For resource creation return stable IDs/status; short-lived presigns are freshly signed on an authorized retry rather than stored. Receipts retain 30 days; durable financial/attendance uniqueness still lives in those domains. **One Django URL pattern/name serves all methods sharing that path**; register protected/OpenAPI entries per (that name,method). Never mount duplicate identical paths solely to invent method-specific names.

Success: GET/PATCH/action 200, create 201, queued batch/render/scan 202 with `{job_id,state,status_url}`, delete/revoke 200 with terminal state for idempotent UI. Preserve old endpoint response shapes. Errors: 400 DRF field errors plus stable code where applicable; 401 unauthenticated; 403 known local insufficient authority; uniform 404 foreign/unknown/hidden; 409 `stale_version/capacity_full/team_locked/invalid_transition/lease_lost/idempotency_conflict` with current authorized version only; 410 known authorized expired asset; 413 limits; 423 source migration freeze; 429 throttle; 503 storage/gate/provider-probe unavailable. No stack/provider response or cross-tenant existence details. Mutation validation ordering preserves existing public/module error behavior.

Prefixes (new route kwarg `pk` always identifies Event for origin lookup; nested IDs are separately validated):

- **M** = `/api/v1/member/makerspaces/{makerspace_id}/events/{pk}`; authenticated member, own application/team/assignment only, host derives from the event. Admission audience is existing member/account/invite policy, not automatically membership-only. Collaborative entry uses durable provenance and matching origin; a foreign maker tenant cannot acquire host-wide rights.
- **A** = `/api/v1/admin/events/{pk}`; existing staff-context/delegate authentication and exact `event_authority` permission. Session/account context is checked by established middleware; member JWT alone is not blanket admin access.
- **P** = `/api/v1/public/event-programmes/{public_token}`; public event/gallery projections with explicit venue target resolution and per-route live gates. The `/context/` owner bootstrap explicitly requires authentication despite this prefix (§12A.2); other projections retain their stated authentication. Existing tenant-slug public event URLs stay compatible. Certificate verify is the separate route in §9.
- **S** = existing `/api/v1/admin/event-series/{pk}` routes for series guest projections, matching inspected `events/urls_admin.py`; no parallel series alias.

Thus A `/application-decisions/release/` is `events-programme-admin-application-decisions-release`; GET/PATCH A `/roles/{assignment_id}/` share `events-programme-admin-roles`, and its `/approve/` is `events-programme-admin-roles-approve`. Collection and detail with identical literals use `-list` and `-detail` respectively to avoid duplicate names; names explicitly listed below override this rule. Expand each brace group into separate named paths in the OpenAPI manifest. ### Asset model and exactly-once storage workflow

`SubmissionAsset` fields: event/submission/team, UUID public_id, kind/group, sanitized original display filename, extension, policy_name/version and frozen effective cap, declared MIME/bytes, canonical MIME/actual bytes, staging key, server-only verification key, final object key, source/final version IDs where available, SHA-256, state, scan backend/status/version/time, ZIP manifest/subtype, duration/dimensions/codecs, uploaded_by, multipart upload ID encrypted or private, generation/claim UUID, last_activity_at, reserved_bytes, charged_bytes, failure_code, ready_at, expires_at, expired_at, deleted_at, expired_size_bytes. `expired_at` marks logical terminal expiry, `deleted_at` confirmed byte cleanup; do not conflate them. Keys are generated by the server under `hackathon/<tenant>/<event>/<team>/<uuid>.<ext>`, staging under `staging/`, and verification under a distinct never-presigned server prefix. Participant assets use member ownership and purpose instead of team with the same expiry fields; the transport accepts a typed owner adapter, never a client-supplied ownership path.

`submissions/asset_workflow.py` is the sole state owner: `reserved→uploading→uploaded→validating→promoting→ready`; failures go to rejected/quarantined/aborted, ready→expiring→expired. Transient validation/promotion failures remain retryable at the same claim/generation. Only ready assets can attach to a snapshot. Immutable ready content cannot be replaced; upload a new asset for a new version. Per-owner count limits apply before presigning, not just at submit.

1. **Initialize**: authenticated active team member or participant owner; validate event window, group/extension, size ≥1, item count and all quota layers under event/usage locks. Persist reservation and audit before I/O. Below 25 MiB use exact staging-only presigned POST with content-length-range; larger uses S3 multipart, 16 MiB default parts increased as necessary to stay ≤10,000 parts. No application-server buffering of large request bodies. Presigns last 15 minutes and are scope/generation-bound.
2. **Resume**: expose only server-issued upload ID and exact part numbers/size range. Sign bounded batches of part URLs, verify row ownership on every refresh. Reconcile uploaded parts using server `list_parts`; never trust client ETag/size list as proof. Do not log returned URLs. Multipart CORS must allow PUT/POST and expose ETag on the configured browser-facing storage origin, preserving the existing Silo/minio service and volume names.
3. **Complete**: completion command is idempotent by asset/generation. Persist a completion claim, call storage outside DB locks, use the server-listed ordered parts, HEAD exact declared size and caps, then copy the completed staging version to the **never client-writable verification key** using version ID or source ETag conditional copy. If source changes, reject/retry; never validate one staging version and promote different bytes. A repeated single PUT cannot alter verification/final bytes. Recheck source gate/ownership/version in a short commit before validation is scheduled.
4. **Validate**: ranged prefix/tail and ZIP central-directory checks below; stream the frozen verification object through SHA-256 and optional ClamAV with constant-memory chunks. Full streaming is needed for hash/scan and bounded image decode/XML checks; it is not permission to load multi-GB objects into RAM. Store only canonical metadata. Reject malformed/hostile content before ready. Images are bounded to one frame, 16 MP, re-encoded with metadata stripped using existing primitives. Hash the actual canonical stored bytes; retain original hash separately if transformed.
5. **Scan and probe**: `HACKATHON_SCAN_BACKEND=none|clamav`; none is explicit skipped, dev default. Production documents recommend clamav. When configured, scanner timeout/unavailable/error blocks ready and retries; it never silently becomes skipped. Infected objects quarantine, lose all read authorization immediately and get deletion work; preserve hashes/status. Enforce clamd INSTREAM size and MaxScanSize/MaxFileSize/MaxRecursion/MaxFiles, and distinguish “not fully scanned” from clean. ffprobe is required for accepted uploaded videos: use non-root worker, bounded temporary disk, memory/CPU/wall-clock, local-file protocols only, no remote URLs and sanitized errors. Validate event duration/resolution bounds (default 30–240 seconds, at least 720p, maximum 4K; organizer may lower within server limits). Save codecs so unsupported browser playback offers original download; no transcode/HLS/thumbnail server is implied.
6. **Promote**: conditional final-key creation from the verified immutable source, with version/checksum verification. If server-side conditional copy is unavailable, stream to a unique server-only destination and use conditional put/multipart completion; never expose destination until its digest matches. Claim/generation CAS ensures only one ready publication and one quota charge. Crash after storage write is reconciled by owned key/hash, not overwritten. Failed/aborted keys remain in durable cleanup work until deleted.
7. **Serve**: use the purpose policy below, never a generic direct GET presign. Ready only; a known owner-authorized expired asset returns 410 **before any storage access**, and unknown/foreign/public-hidden assets return uniform 404. Set safe attachment disposition, canonical MIME, no-store and nosniff. Gated media supports single `Range`, 206/416/Content-Range and reauthorizes every range; it never returns a reusable storage redirect. HTML/SVG/source/archives are never inline on the app origin. URLs/keys never enter stored content, logs, public page documents or analytics.
8. **Cleanup**: abort multipart idle >24 hours (also configure bucket incomplete-multipart lifecycle); clean unattached draft assets 30 days after event close, earlier owner deletion if unreferenced; remove staging/verification copies promptly after successful promotion. Expire all canonical versions, retained staging versions, verification objects and preview copies at event retention deadline. Database expiry blocks reads before deletion and retries physical cleanup. Keep rows, checksums, manifest and snapshots. Release reservations or charged quota **only after all owned bytes/parts are confirmed removed**, with idempotent usage receipts. No snapshotted asset metadata row deletion by draft cleanup.

Network I/O and task attempts carry existing request/log correlation outside audit metadata. Worker temp files are deleted on completion/failure; no object keys or raw filenames in provider error strings. Background tasks use persisted work records and sweeper recovery even without Celery beat (register equivalent cloud scheduler jobs in deployment writer inventory).

### Download purposes, expiry and revocation guarantees

`submissions/read_policy.py` has a closed purpose enum; the caller cannot choose a less restrictive purpose through a query parameter. Server route/actor determines it. B owns the event reader/policy adapter; G's always-present `makerspaces/private_upload_transport.py` owns shared model-free streaming/expiry primitives, E/P/F own their subject gateways. Accounts never imports Events to stream its vault/export bytes. Unknown purpose fails closed. All programme participant bytes are **gated streaming**, including a participant's own originals; there is no private-submission direct-presign exception to remember.

| Private/public purpose | Transport and authorization at every request |
| --- | --- |
| Team draft/submitted original, source/archive download, preview or video | Gated authenticated stream; current eligible team member and exact draft/frozen snapshot. Leaving/removal/withdrawal ends access synchronously. Historical owner access, if permitted by existing accountability policy, is a separately checked owner-history purpose, never stale team membership. |
| Application reviewer/judge submission reads | Gated authenticated stream; current live grant/role and assigned application or round/frozen snapshot, nonconflicted, in valid window. Reviewer projections never gain unrelated project/resume access. Assignment loss denies an old app URL. |
| Organizer/moderator private assets | Gated authenticated stream; exact current event permission, tenant/source/feature/standing; no permission from a prior export or URL issuance. |
| Sponsor track originals / participant résumé | Gated authenticated stream; active rep grant/assignment and exact submission track. Résumé also needs that participant's active consent for this sponsor **and that exact asset revision**. Revoke/replace/track loss ends new bytes immediately. Mentors have no implicit submission/résumé access; any permitted help attachment is separately gated by current assignment. |
| Public gallery originals, previews, video, event card photos | Gated no-store stream; publication/current consent/item eligibility/host/module/source-profile predicates at every request. No storage-key redirect. Public reads of expired bytes return no bytes even if gallery JSON is cached. |
| Saved résumé originals, owner Saved details export and owner personal-data archive | Owner-authenticated gated stream; active account/key readiness and object ready/unexpired. No anonymous archive URL in notifications. |
| Private certificate PDF and badge/ID PDF, print resources | Gated stream; current owner or authorized staff subject predicate; active certificate state where required, print/credential/photo consent generation and authority checks as §§9/9A. Certificate document delivery uses its separate one-use provider grant, not a reusable presign. |
| Nonparticipant certificate-library/template artwork originals and dummy design previews | **Deliberately bounded bearer GET**, maximum 60 seconds, only after current designer/library authority. No member photos, submitted files, certificates, badge PDFs, real QR, answers or résumé may enter this class. Revoking designer authority after issuance may leave these already issued immutable design-artwork bytes readable until the stated deadline. UI/docs state this bounded window. Rendering can instead use internal SDK reads without issuing a client URL. |
| Provider PDF fetch | Typed, one-use gateway grant bound to recipient/delivery/integration/document revision, max 60 seconds and provider authority window; revalidate source at consumption and during streaming. No provider-direct object presign. |
| Existing scheduled report delivery outside this new asset engine | Preserve the explicitly documented existing read-only bounded-bearer contract (default 6h) and its own report expiry; do not silently convert it or claim instantaneous report-link revocation in this programme. No résumé/submission/badge export is routed through that exception. |

For every bounded URL **and gateway fetch grant**, compute `not_after = min(now+purpose_max_ttl, object.expires_at, event_asset_expiry, role/grant/entitlement.valid_until, assignment.ends_at, round.closes_at when access ends then, consent.expires_at, print_job.expires_at, provider_window_end)` using only applicable limits. A limit with no configured end is omitted, never used to override a finite other end. Infrastructure/session credential expiry also bounds S3 signing; floor TTL to whole seconds and refuse if ≤0. Newly ready objects inherit the event's existing retention deadline, so late/correction uploads cannot gain a fresh TTL. Gateway paths still reauthorize dynamically even before `not_after`; bounding is not a substitute for live revocation. Upload-part presigns are write-only staging permissions, independently bounded by upload generation/window and cannot expose final objects.

Gateway URLs are resource locators, not bearer permissions: copying one to another actor/browser cannot confer access. Check DB-backed live authority and consent without a stale positive cache; public cached shells are not authority. On an active transfer, read at most 1 MiB or 2 seconds (whichever comes first) between policy checks, hold the one chunk until recheck, and stop on revocation/expiry/source freeze before sending the next chunk. Already sent or kernel-buffered bytes cannot be recalled; “immediate revocation” means the next authorized request/chunk fails, not erasure of data already downloaded. Do not hold DB row locks for the stream's lifetime. HEAD obtains identical authorization and no secret content. A multi-range request is 416; no-store excludes protected bytes from PWA/CDN/browser caches under app control.

Acceptance **must issue URLs before the change**: start with a team owner, remove them; issue judge link then reassign/close round; issue sponsor résumé link then revoke consent or replace asset/remove track; issue public gallery/photo link then withdraw consent/profile; issue badge PDF link then rotate credential/revoke photo; issue provider grant then revoke certificate/integration. Assert old gateway GET/HEAD/Range returns uniform denial and no storage call, ongoing transfer halts at next chunk, with warm cache and Redis unavailable. Separately issue a template-artwork bounded presign, revoke authority, demonstrate it can read until `not_after` and fails afterward using storage-backed expiry tests; new sign requests must deny immediately. Assert URL expiry is capped by each finite object/authority boundary including sub-60-second windows and 410 never contacts storage. Do not write an unrealistic test expecting a direct S3 presign to consult the current DB.
