No server office conversion, macro execution or mechanical toolpath execution.

### Ranged ZIP listing and browser resource bounds

Implement seekable `S3RangeReader` against the **frozen verification object**, validating Content-Range/length and bounding reads. Read EOCD tail, ZIP64 locator/records when present, then central directory ≤1 MiB. ZIP64 is either fully bounds-validated or rejected with a typed unsupported-container error; do not overflow integers. Never `.open()`/extract entries on server. ZIP-based formats share this validator. Store a bounded manifest of sanitized entry names, sizes, kinds and nested-archive flags; individual filenames remain private unless that asset is public.

Reject encrypted entries, >2,000 entries, duplicate normalized paths, absolute paths, `..`, backslashes, drive/UNC/control-character names, symlinks, inconsistent/overlapping offsets, directory outside object, total declared expansion >1 GiB or >20× compressed size, any entry >100:1, lying local-vs-central header sizes (read local headers in bounded ranges; handle valid data descriptors explicitly), and appended polyglots such as PNG+ZIP. Containers with required entries are checked by directory metadata; do not pretend a listing validates all inner semantics. Nested archives are listed/flagged, not recursively unpacked. ClamAV archive scanning is separately sandboxed and bounded. Format XML inside a compressed container is not server parsed just to make a preview.

Initial required previews: lazy three.js STL/OBJ/3MF (ask before loading ≥50 MiB), occt-import-js STEP/IGES only on click, tracespace Gerber/drill with output caps. Run parsers in terminateable workers with compressed/decompressed byte, facet/vertex, entry, memory and time limits; keep the original download available if preview fails. No external model texture URLs. Render generated SVG via safe image/sandbox with CSP, never insert untrusted SVG markup in app DOM. Add appropriate package notices and lazy chunks; KiCad and server thumbnail rendering remain later. Previews are not validation or a reason to reject a valid download-only maker asset.

### Quota and retention accounting

- Managed SaaS dedicated hackathon allowance = **25,000,000,000 bytes per hackathon event**. Do not accidentally intersect it with the old tenant base 1 GiB allowance. Add a typed event storage pool/reservation through `limits_reservations.py`/`limits_usage.py`: charge total tenant/provider usage for accounting but apply the hackathon entitlement pool to these objects, not the ordinary base pool. No online-payment-module dependency for a storage entitlement. A budget reduction below used+reserved is refused; it never deletes submissions.
- Self-host event budget is null/unlimited by default; organizer can set a finite local budget. Security per-file, per-submission and upload-count ceilings remain even when event storage has no billing limit. Surface used/reserved/available and failed-cleanup bytes to staff.
- Group totals per submission: video 500 MiB (configurable within server ceiling), deck 50, images 50, source 200, PCB 150, CAD 500, firmware 50, fab-2d 150, fab-3dprint 500, fab-cnc 300, embroidery 50, archives 200; total **1.5 GiB**. Group caps supersede individual caps where smaller. Count an asset once against storage even when referenced by several snapshots; count all uploaded versions and pending reservations for quota. Each event policy can lower these caps, including default video requirements for a hardware track. Source ZIP and generic ZIP are categorized by slot to avoid double counting.
- Reserve declared bytes atomically before signing; promotion converts reservation to canonical actual bytes once, keyed by asset UUID. Smaller re-encoded images release the difference only after discarded bytes disappear. Storage initialization failure queues abort/cleanup then releases when confirmed; never leave an untracked multipart upload. Quota, signer, completion and worker crashes have compensating work and idempotent receipts.
- Retention expiry is independent of feature enablement, gallery publication, public/private choice and module removal. Register retained metadata ownership and expiry locators even under tombstoning. Backups/tenant captures tolerate **expected expired absence**, but treat missing ready unexpired bytes as corruption. Import preserves source expiry timestamps and cannot revive expired files. Previously exported backups may contain historical bytes under the existing backup retention policy; document that distinction and enforce expiry again on restore, rather than claiming deletion retroactively erases backups.
sections.credentials_and_photos:
Badge/ID check-in credentials and certificate verification

### Badge token design — resolved

Add `EventRegistrationCredential(registration FK, generation, token_digest unique, token_ciphertext, key_version, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, revoked_by, revocation_reason)`, one unrevoked generation per registration; and a registration `credential_mode legacy/v2`. Digest is deployment-keyed HMAC of a cryptographically random 256-bit secret with domain separation `event-registration:v2` and the **selected event ID**. Resolution can therefore compute it before knowing the registration, then require that the credential's registration belongs to that event; do not include an unknown registration ID in a digest lookup formula. The immutable registration FK provides per-registration binding. Recoverable raw secret is encrypted using the deployment credential key solely to reproduce an owner's QR/authorized badge print; it is never stored as plaintext or portable data. Model encryption/secret catalogues explicitly distinguish this from ordinary PII. Ciphertext, digest, mode/generation and revocation are handled by credential services, not template merge tags.

QR payload is `SWEC2.<opaque-secret>` (no member ID, email, name, tenant ID or public-profile handle). Staff scanner has an already-selected event; POST body supplies the payload, so credentials do not enter URL/access logs, referrers, analytics or public links. Digest lookup requires that event, this registration and current live generation. Scan cannot be used at another event or to authenticate/enter another system. A token can resolve repeatedly during its valid event window for identity, while attendance confirmation is idempotent and refuses a second attendance transition. “Not reusable across events” does not prohibit scanning an attended badge to identify its owner at that same event.

`events/credentials/workflow.py` owns issue/rotate/revoke/expire. Owner ticket/QR display and authorized badge print share **the same current event credential**. A full manager or `check_in` operator with the dedicated rotate action can revoke a lost card and issue its replacement, auditing IDs/generation only. Cancellation/rejection/withdrawal/expired admission and event cancellation revoke synchronously; grant revocation prevents the former helper from scanning without invalidating attendees. Never resurrect a revoked generation on restore/cancel undo; reissue explicitly. Ticket identity requires a real member-bound registration; legacy account-less/unbound rows use existing desk handling and cannot become a fabricated member identity.

V2 resolution requires authenticated active staff or member delegate with live `check_in` for the selected event, valid Host/Origin, source gate, event/credential scan window and module. Return minimal `{registration_id, member_id, name, status, attended_at, ticket_type_name, host_waiver_state, confirmable, credential_generation}`; member ID stays staff-only. Preserve existing stricter payment/answer visibility: check-in-only helpers do not acquire payment details, contact or custom answers. Waiver state is the existing two-location helper; scan reports it without inventing another gate. Separate confirm calls existing `services_checkin.mark_attended_with_event` with operation UUID; credential resolution never marks attendance or presence itself. Existing presence bridge keeps its exact conditions.

V2 is **online-only** to guarantee revocation. Staff offline roster never downloads raw v2 credentials or identity secrets; it shows “Reconnect to verify this badge.” Existing legacy offline-ticket protocol remains for registrations still in legacy mode with its existing leases/replay handling. Issuing v2 disables all legacy UUID QR resolve/sync paths for that registration, so an old offline roster cannot bypass revocation after reconnect. New hackathon registrations use v2; ordinary legacy events opt into v2 when issuing a new QR badge/ticket, with an explicit replacement notice and reprint. Existing bare UUID tickets are not silently reinterpreted as public identity. Update member ticket PNG/SVG, badge PDF and scanner components together.

Private ticket GET may show attended state/QR for same-event staff identity while `confirmable=false`. Polling/SSE stub tear is decorative; reloading reads persisted attendance. Returned QR is no-store, owner/print-action scoped, not service-worker cached. Never include live QR secrets in design preview, test cards, exports, reports, chat PDFs or audit. Test badge uses an unmistakably nonresolving dummy pattern. Ordinary member cards retain their separate protocol and authority.

### Certificate subject model and one issuance pipeline

Extend existing `EventAttendanceCertificate` rather than build a parallel certificate table. Add explicit event FK (backfilled from registration), recipient_member FK (nullable for retained legacy identity), kind `attendance/participant/finalist/winner/volunteer_thanks/mentor_thanks/judge_thanks`, optional role_assignment and award/result_revision, `public_verification_enabled`, and an opaque verification ID (reuse existing random `serial`). Make feedback response nullable and registration nullable **only** under a DB subject-shape CHECK: registration subject or role-assignment subject, exactly one; response, when present, must belong to that registration. A result award must match event/team/recipient. Existing feedback flow stays attendance+response; bulk attendance does not create fake feedback.

Replace old global “one nonrevoked certificate per registration” with subject+kind+award uniqueness, retaining one live attendance certificate per registration and distinct winner certificates per legitimate prize. Migrate revision uniqueness to an explicitly versioned subject+kind+award key, retaining old attendance revision values and updating every existing consumer together. Use DB validation/trigger guards for event/subject/response/artwork consistency. Recipient-name/event/date/layout/hash snapshots remain immutable; `revoked_by` is attribution only. Abstract read/ownership through `events/certificates/subjects.py` so download, envelopes, history, export, rendering and origin scope do not dereference a nullable registration blindly.

`services_certificates.py` remains the workflow facade: pending→rendering→active/failed, failed→rendering retry, active→revoked; reissue creates a new immutable certificate revision. Extend to bulk by persisted `CertificateIssueBatch` and item rows (unique batch+subject+kind+award, chunk size 100). Full manager previews eligibility/count, confirms “issue to all attended” or selected verified contributions, then batch uses identical individual issuance. Duplicate retries do not reissue. Attendance correction/event cancellation revokes appropriate certificate subjects through the same service. Result corrections flag/revoke superseded awards explicitly. Contribution certificate requires verified hours/approved contribution; self-reported hours are insufficient.

### Public verification, distinct from PDF access

Add public SPA `/certificates/verify/<uuid>` and typed GET `/api/v1/public/event-certificates/<uuid>/verify/`. QR in issued PDF encodes the canonical verification URL; printed ID is the same unguessable UUID. It grants no PDF or member access. A known opted-in issued certificate returns exactly `{event, date, status: valid|revoked}`; no recipient name/ID, email, issuer contact, score, hours, file URL or revocation reason. Invalid/unknown/not-yet-issued/private-verification-disabled yields uniform 404. Rate-limit and use no-store/nosniff; GET is read-only and must not create a per-view audit trail.

New issuance defaults public verification on with event/date-only disclosure stated in the issuance UI; legacy issued certificates default off until a full manager explicitly enables verification. Event title/date disclosure is a separate explicit certificate-publication policy, applicable even for an otherwise private or ended event. Tenant servability, runtime/module and verification withdrawal still gate every request. Event-page expiry and `is_public=False` do not implicitly remove a deliberately published certificate verification, nor allow wider event fields. Public verification of a revoked certificate remains “revoked” while opt-in is retained. PDFs, recipient identity and rendering artwork remain private under existing owner/staff authority. Tombstoning Events removes the verification runtime route; retained archive rows remain intact.

## 9A. Decision 33 — selected membership profile, photo consent and badge rendering

`makerspaces.MemberProfile` belongs to **one MakerspaceMembership**, not to the account; `avatar_key` is already uploaded through `makerspaces/profile_images.py` to the public-image bucket. Reuse that existing upload and photo. Do not introduce a second badge-photo upload, staff profile, global account avatar, staff-account lookup, camera capture requirement or private member-card photo source. Existing source-bucket URLs may already be public; this programme cannot retroactively make a previously copied URL/printed photo private. It controls new event disclosure, live card access and new printing.

E owns `events/profile_photos/{models,selection_workflow,policy,projection,snapshot,serializers,views,urls_member,urls_public}.py`. Add `EventMemberPresentation(event,member,selected_profile FK nullable,selected_membership FK nullable,print_photo_consent=false,public_card_consent=false,public_card_scopes=[],consent_revision,consented_at,revoked_at,version)` unique(event,member). Both FKs must refer to the same membership and to the actor's own active member account; all setters use the owner-only service. The account's list of selectable profiles includes explicit membership ID, profile ID, venue name, avatar availability, public eligibility and source revision; no preselection, even for a single membership. “No photo/profile” is always a visible valid choice. A previous event's choice, PublicHandle.profile, browser's selected venue and first matching membership are **never** defaults. Choice is per event, with the source membership stated next to the preview; it conveys no host/source tenant authority.

For a cross-venue participant, allow choosing an owned active profile at another venue only after an explicit selection showing both source venue and destination event, with independent print/public-card checkboxes off by default. Validate source membership active, source membership module and source tenant servability on selection **and each use**. Do not require joining the host or create a profile when event audience permits account-only applicants. No profile, missing photo, inactive/removed membership, disabled source module, removed avatar or inaccessible source yields a branded silhouette/initials from the already authorized event name for a private badge; no new image URL is fetched and no other membership is substituted. Staff accounts have no profile choice. A staff operational row can have its permitted role label and placeholder, but never a public member card generated from staff private data.

Print consent is solely “Use this selected profile photo on this event's badge/ID card”; it does not publish a profile, grant sponsor/résumé use or public-card consent. Public-card consent is separately granted for explicit `team`, `mentor`, `judge` scopes at this event; it does not grant print consent. Setting a different profile resets both consents/scopes and increments revision; avatar changes invalidate pending photo snapshots and require a fresh render using current selected source, without silently choosing another source. Owner can revoke either consent without withdrawing attendance/role. Public scope inclusion additionally requires team/project or role `display_on_page` consent, the chosen profile's current `profile_is_public` predicate, and the canonical handle still referring to **that same profile**. A private/withdrawn profile or handle move removes the public card/link immediately; do not reuse a saved display name/avatar or redirect to a different membership. Public card payload is an allowlist of current public display name, chosen skills/role, canonical public link and gated event photo URL (nullable); no membership ID, private affiliation, phone, email or registration ID. No photo with otherwise eligible public profile yields a placeholder. D's team/gallery projections and C's mentor/judge providers call the same E policy; pages team sections use this projection too.

Public photos use GET `P /member-cards/{card_public_id}/photo/` through the event gateway; it checks all live source/profile/consent/host/gallery-or-page gates and streams safe image bytes, no redirect to public storage key. Keep no-store/nosniff and omit keys/source venue IDs from public JSON. This is a narrow event disclosure adapter over an owner-selected foreign profile, not permission to navigate its tenant-specific profile API; canonical cross-venue public links use the existing platform canonical profile URL and its own access checks. Revocation denies newly initiated gateway reads with uniform 404 and removes card JSON; it cannot erase a browser's previously received image. Private team/assignment rosters use no selected photo unless the subject explicitly consented to that surface; this plan adds no private roster-photo purpose, so they use placeholders. Desk printing alone may use print-consented source photos.

Replace existing two-field `services_badges.BadgeSnapshot` with a typed immutable in-memory/short-lived job snapshot: `registration_id,event_id,member_id,authorized_fields,template_revision,stock,logo_artwork_revision,credential_generation,credential_render_handle,presentation_id,presentation_version,source_profile_id,source_avatar_revision,photo_sha256,photo_render_handle,created_at,expires_at`. QR and photo are typed render resources, **never** text merge tags or caller URLs. No raw QR secret, raw object key or photo bytes in JSON, database job response, logs, export or task broker. Credential secrets are unwrapped only inside the authorized rendering process; photo retrieval reads the exact server-owned source key/version, bounded-decodes/re-encodes and stages an immutable private render copy outside row locks. Revalidate source avatar hash/revision and consent under fences/event locks before binding the job; if changed restart preparation, if revoked cancel (`409 photo_consent_changed`) or offer a new explicitly no-photo print job. No network I/O under locks.

Render resources are typed `BadgePrintResource` rows/handles with owned private key/hash, print-job binding, expiry ≤24h and durable cleanup. They are coordination, excluded from tenant artifacts/portable User closure; retention ownership remains registered for backup/purge cleanup. `badge_rendering.py` accepts only this snapshot and a server-owned resource resolver; it delegates geometry to the existing printable engine but explicitly renders photo/logo/QR slots with fit/crop bounds and long-name fallback. The old renderer's “no bearer credential” assertion is narrowly superseded **only for authorized event badge rendering**; generic printable layouts never accept credential fields. G owns changes to `operations/printable_pdf.py`/layout seams, E owns the Events renderer. Preview/import/export uses dummy portraits and a nonresolving QR; actual render jobs require `check_in`, real eligible registrations and current print consent for photos. `manage_registrations`+`VIEW_AUDIT` remains required for extra answer fields.

Each print request locks/finalizes permitted snapshots and versions, renders outside locks, then rechecks current authorization, consent, source, credential generation and event window before returning/streaming the PDF. Check again on **each later job PDF GET**; revocation cancels unpublished jobs and denies new reads of already rendered bytes, expiring owned PDFs/resources promptly. Batch jobs authorize each row and report safe row failures rather than substituting another person's photo; no-photo rows still print. Snapshot immutability ensures identical prepared pixels/geometry within a valid job; a new print after avatar/template/QR change makes a new snapshot. Existing downloaded/printed paper cannot be recalled. Badge PDF is owner/authorized-desk gated streaming, never chat attachment or bounded public bearer URL. Tests include two distinct venue avatars, account-only member, staff account, inactive source, no photo, consent toggles, source deletion/change during render, old job URL after revocation, cross-tenant origin, long names and photo+logo+physical-size scannable QR at every supported stock.
sections.saved_details:
Binding additions 28/30 — account-owned Saved details and registration autofill

This is a **private account-owned vault**, separate from tenant `MemberProfile` publication and separate from login identity fields (`phone_e164`, verified email). A member with no membership can use it. No organizer, staff grant, sponsor, organization governor or platform UI can browse another account's vault. Only values the member explicitly submits to a specific event become that organizer's answer snapshot. Event registration cannot silently overwrite verified login identifiers or public profile consent.

### Models, encryption and ownership

- `accounts/saved_details/models.py::MemberSavedDetail(user,field_key,value_envelope,value_type,version,updated_at,save_consent_version,consented_at)`, unique(user,field_key); member-kind only. Standard keys: name, phone, institution, organization, study_level, country ISO, skills, github_url, linkedin_url, portfolio_url, resume, shirt_size, dietary_needs, accessibility_needs, emergency_contact, **date_of_birth**. Keys have typed bounds, sensitive/default-save metadata and canonicalization; arbitrary custom form labels never become vault keys. A standard key can be linked by a custom question only through validated `profile_field_key`/type compatibility in forms_schema v2.
- `MemberSavedAsset(user,public_id,object_key,staging_key,verification_key,sha256,size_bytes,canonical_mime,state,scan_status,version,created_at)` for saved resume; PDF only, ≤10 MiB, explicit owner upload and scan policy. Reuse B's **model-free, always-present** upload transport primitives extracted into `makerspaces/private_upload_transport.py`, with account-owned adapter/workflow and a bounded 50 MiB account vault asset budget (self-host may configure more; preserve per-file safety cap). Accounts must not import Events to upload or read saved details. Distinct private account prefix, never charge/own it under the last visited event. Retired resume bytes are deleted after replacement when no vault reference remains; event submission copies have independent ownership/retention.
- The current scoped-PII registry/crypto is tenant-specific (`makerspace:<id>` AAD); **do not fake a makerspace** for private global saved details. Add `encryption/account_{registry,crypto,mappers,services}.py` with explicit owner scope `account`, `AccountPiiKey(user,version,wrapped_dek,broker_backend,broker_key_id,status)`, unique user+version and one active key. Reuse existing AES-256-GCM/wrapped-DEK broker primitives with new versioned AAD `account:<user_id>:<table>:<pk>:<field>`, distinct `pii:account:gcm:v1` envelope, account-bound broker context and no plaintext fallback. Existing tenant crypto/envelopes stay compatible. Apply fail-closed account mapper, raw/bulk-write prohibition, key-unavailable behavior and account/global write-fence checks/system registration guard. Encrypt all vault values, particularly DOB/dietary/accessibility/emergency contact; no blind index/search over them. New account key row is a deployment-secret model, excluded from tenant export/closure; ordinary deployment recovery preserves its wrapped-key custody.
- After the source and global→account PII fences, owner `User`→account key→detail/asset rows (sorted) is the account-only mutation order. A frozen unrelated tenant does not freeze the vault. `SavedDetailUpdateIntent(user,operation_uuid,event_id,subject_kind,subject_id,base_versions,chosen_fields,encrypted_payload,key_version,key_epoch,state pending/applied/conflict/failed,created_at,expires_at)` is inserted atomically with the successful registration/application command using the preparation protocol below. Postcommit account service applies under account-only locks. No event command takes account row locks. Conflicts preserve newer vault values; retries expose “review saved details” status. A rolled-back event leaves no intent. Completed/conflicted payloads are erased within 24h; pending payloads expire after 7 days and become `failed` with `save_intent_expired`, requiring explicit owner resubmission. Minimal safe receipt/status survives 30 days. A worker/storage failure after a successful event commit never rolls admission back or reports the event submission as failed.
- Account deletion removes vault rows, intents, owned resume objects/all versions and account encryption keys through explicit reviewed erasure path/cache eviction. Do not reuse tenant keys' undeletable manager in a way that blocks mandated account erasure. Retain only non-PII deletion receipts required for retryable byte cleanup. Already submitted event answers remain under existing accountability/retention policy and are explained in deletion UI; organizers cannot read deleted vault values via old references.

### Autofill and save semantics

The model-free field descriptor below is the shared F-owned `forms_schema/profile_fields.py` contract. All vault values are encrypted; “sensitive” here governs save defaults and UI disclosure, not encryption on/off. Strings normalize Unicode/trim safely; blank never means delete. Profile mapping supports only compatible primitive types; do not coerce a choice label into another form's option ID. The nonpersistable age descriptor cannot be PUT as a vault field.

| Standard key | Canonical value / bound | Sensitive / default save |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string ≤200 | no / on |
| `phone` | string ≤32 normalized international contact number, no login verification mutation | no / on |
| `institution`, `organization` | strings ≤200 each | no / on |
| `study_level` | string ≤100, open text rather than institution-specific enum | no / on |
| `country` | uppercase ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 | no / on |
| `skills` | distinct ordered strings ≤50 tags, each ≤60 chars | no / on |
| `github_url`, `linkedin_url`, `portfolio_url` | HTTPS URL ≤2048, no credentials, no fetch | no / on |
| `shirt_size` | string ≤32; prefill only if valid in receiving form's choices | no / on |
| `dietary_needs`, `accessibility_needs` | string ≤2000 each; mapped text input only | yes / off |
| `emergency_contact` | `{name:string≤200,relationship:string≤100,phone:string≤32}` from typed compound field; no relationship inference | yes / off |
| `resume` | typed ready owner account asset reference `{asset_id:int,sha256:string}`, never a URL/object key | yes / off |
| `date_of_birth` | ISO calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`, valid and not future | yes / off |
| `age_at_event` | derived informational descriptor only; accepts a DOB source in §12A, no saved value | derived / never saved |

V2 also supports the typed `emergency_contact` compound question and maps only the compound key; v1 consumers remain unchanged. A custom field maps to one descriptor and its allowed type; duplicate active mappings require identical canonical value or reject `duplicate_profile_mapping`. Choice mappings (shirt size/study level) validate received option IDs against the receiving schema before suggesting a value; otherwise owner gets an unfilled draft and can choose. Do not persist age, foreign résumé references or choices from invisible questions.

#### Always encrypted account vault: provisioning, readiness and preparation

Account encryption is independent of `PII_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED` (currently false by default) and cannot inherit its plaintext mode. G adds `ACCOUNT_SAVED_DETAILS_ENABLED` (off until configured), `ACCOUNT_PII_KEY_BROKER=local|aws_kms`, `ACCOUNT_PII_MASTER_KEY`, `ACCOUNT_PII_MASTER_KEY_PREVIOUS`, and `ACCOUNT_PII_AWS_KMS_KEY_ID` to settings/env/backup secret policy. Local uses a separately generated 32-byte wrapping secret; KMS uses an explicit key and account-bound encryption context. Never reuse audit/search/token keys. Deployment readiness requires a valid broker configuration and successful bounded wrap/unwrap health probe before advertising vault save/prefill. Configuration checks run even when tenant PII is disabled; enabled+missing/invalid key is an actionable system-check failure. Dev/test runners provision disposable secrets explicitly, production install provisions/persists the secret through the existing secret store; neither frontend nor request code invents a replacement key. Lost key/readiness reports unavailable; no plaintext writes, cleartext columns, empty-key encryption or silent loss of saved values. Final deployment acceptance enables the configured vault rather than leaving decision 28 dormant.

`prepare_saved_detail_intent(actor,event_context,validated_form,choices,base_versions,operation_id)` runs before the event transaction. It validates member ownership, schema hash/version, subject kind, visible normalized answers, size limits and explicit sensitive choices; allocates intent UUID/AAD in advance. First-use key creation uses a short account-only transaction to claim a provisioning record under account fences/User lock; generate/wrap DEK outside locks; finalize under the same account order with CAS. A parallel creator reuses the winner; crash/stale claim retries, no orphan active key and no KMS I/O in a DB transaction. Readiness is not first-use key readiness: a missing/unwrappable per-account key returns `503 account_key_unavailable` before any event row lock or mutation. A preparing concurrent caller gets retryable `409 account_key_preparing` with Retry-After. Unavailable vault with nonempty save choices returns `503 saved_details_unavailable`; the UI preserves the form and offers an explicit new submission with all save choices false. Never silently change a true choice to false.

The preparation result is an in-process, nonclient capability containing immutable encrypted payload, intent UUID, key version/epoch, owner/event/subject binding, canonical-answer hash, form hash and 60-second preparation deadline. Intent PK is that preallocated UUID, so its row/field AAD is known before INSERT. For a new auto-increment subject whose PK does not yet exist, bind preparation to `(event,owner,subject_kind,creation_operation_uuid)`; the service sets its actual typed FK after creating the subject under event locks and verifies the same operation receipt/owner. Existing subjects bind their actual PK. Do not reserve DB IDs with an account lock or re-encrypt against a different PK in the event transaction. It is not a stored plaintext draft, bearer API token or logged value. Tenant keys required by the event-encrypted answer/derivation fields are also prepared/unwrapped outside event row locks under their existing broker protocol. Event command: acquire §4 fences, reject stale/erased account epoch (`409 account_key_changed`) or expired context (`409 save_preparation_expired`), lock domain, revalidate form/date/version/visible-answer hash and consent, then insert the **prepared ciphertext only** with the actual typed subject reference. Schema/date changes return the relevant 409 and restart preparation. No opportunistic key creation or KMS cache miss can run in a mapper under event locks; it raises a retryable preparation error and rolls the transaction back. A command receipt for an earlier successful operation is checked before preparing again, so retrying a committed submission does not resubmit because a key later became unavailable.

Worker application rechecks account active/member kind, exclusive erasure state, key epoch, intent expiry and base versions. Rotation may admit a retained prior epoch only through the explicit authorized rotation chain; otherwise mark for account-only re-encryption/retry, never try a random key/plaintext. Retain decryptable prior versions until intents finish/expire or migrate them in that maintenance job; erased accounts cancel pending intents before key destruction. No deleted vault value is resurrected by an old intent: per-field deletion leaves a version/tombstone until pending intents expire. GET intent status returns safe per-field `applied/conflict/failed` and current versions only, never plaintext payload or key material. Fault tests cover first-use, two creators, broker timeout, prepared→erase/rotation, event rollback, worker failure and resume after restore.

`accounts/saved_details/workflow.py` owns create/update/delete/resume lifecycle; `forms_schema/profile_fields.py` owns the well-known typed key registry. Add nonpersistable derived key `age_at_event`, distinct from saved `date_of_birth`; form v2 recognizes it as an informational derived question, never a generic saved numeric field, and rejects age-range admission rules. Event/hackathon/volunteer/mentor forms call the same owner-only prefill endpoint with a validated schema/event context and receive only requested mapped keys. Sensitive saved fields are inserted into a **reviewable draft**, never automatically submitted or revealed to the organizer. Per-field “Save to my profile” defaults on for non-sensitive keys and **off** for DOB, resume, dietary/accessibility/emergency-contact fields until explicit user opt-in. Record per-field choice; no global default silently opts sensitive fields in. Existing saved sensitive value may prefill for its owner but its save/overwrite choice is still explicit.

On successful submit, copy answers into the event's encrypted canonical snapshot and enqueue only ticked save choices from fields currently visible/answered. Hidden values are removed by form validation and cannot be saved from stale browser payload. Unticking means do not save this new value; deleting an existing saved item is a distinct clear action on Saved details (or explicit “remove saved value”), not inferred from an empty form. A custom question must opt into a valid standard key; type mismatch/duplicate conflicting mapping rejected. Names/phones update the vault, not login identifiers or every historical application. Resume selection copies the ready checked vault object to a **fresh event-owned participant asset** through B's server copy/finalization adapter, increments event quota and freezes hashes; deleting vault resume later cannot remove an event's already-submitted evidence, and sponsor access still needs separate purpose consent.

### DOB and derived age — no stored age

Only DOB is saved, encrypted and opt-in. The age field is a **derived projection**, not a DB column, persistent JSON answer, log/audit value or cached yearly value. `saved_details/age.py::age_on(dob,local_event_start_date)` computes completed calendar years; for Feb 29 birth use March 1 in non-leap years, documented/tested consistently. Reject an invalid/future DOB, but impose no minimum age or minor classification. As-of date is `Event.starts_at` converted to **event timezone**, not UTC date or today's date. Ordinary account Saved details can show current computed age without saving it.

Event derivation source DOB must also remain encrypted: P's derivation service requires usable host-scoped key/envelope support before accepting an age/DOB source; if unavailable return `503 event_pii_unavailable` before event mutation, with a clear readiness action. Never write a raw DOB just because the deployment's existing tenant-PII flag is off. G enables/configures existing tenant PII through its supported staged rollout (including its search readiness prerequisites) for tenants offering these questions; do not toggle it lazily in a registration request or fake an account key as a tenant key. Normal forms without DOB/derived age and explicit no-vault-save submission keep their existing availability. This is separate from the always-encrypted account vault readiness check.

When a form asks age, final review shows computed age and “as of event start” date, explains that source DOB is privately retained to derive that answer, and offers optional save-to-vault (off by default). Without saved DOB collect it privately for derivation; never accept a numeric age to persist. `EventAnswerDerivation(event,registration FK nullable,application FK nullable,role_assignment FK nullable,question_id,source_dob_envelope,event_date_revision,as_of_date,locked_at,version)` has **exactly one of all three subjects** by DB CHECK and three conditional unique(subject,question_id) constraints. All FKs must match the same event and member; the role subject is `EventRoleAssignment`, not an invented attendee registration. `owner_member_id` is obtained from that typed subject and is checked for every write/read/export; only that member may supply/revise its DOB. P owns the model/owner resolver/workflow/serialization; C calls it for volunteer/mentor applications, A for hackathon applications and G's registration adapter for ordinary registrations. Staff cannot insert another member's DOB as part of approval/on-behalf admission.

Age-only canonical answers store `{id,type:"age_at_event",derivation_id}` and schema metadata, never numeric age or source DOB. Own and organizer response serializers compute numeric `value` only at the response/report boundary. Organizer age output is `{id:"age",type:"age_at_event",value:22,as_of_date:"2026-12-01",locked:false}`; source DOB, account references and encryption details are omitted in admin/application/role/check-in/reviewer/sponsor payloads. Blind/disclosure policy may omit even this age answer. An explicitly visible `date_of_birth` question is a separate encrypted answer, disclosed only according to its schema and ordinary private-answer authority; checking “save DOB” is never permission to reveal it. Reports/templates cannot dereference derivation source DOB, and there is no arbitrary derivation GET for staff. Owner event-answer export includes source DOB, subject kind/ID, question, as-of date and locked state through an owner-only export adapter; the global Saved details archive includes **only vault** data, not all tenant event records. The existing owner personal-data export composes both adapters explicitly. Tenant fidelity export preserves encrypted derivation source just like other submitted event PII, with typed subject remap; staff CSV/report exports compute permitted age only.

`Event.event_date_revision` starts at 1; G's single event update path increments it when `starts_at` **or `timezone_name`** changes, including series regeneration/copy-on-write edits, not on unrelated end/title/accent edits. Unlocked derivation projections use the current event-local start date; no materialized computed-age cache. Source DOB changes only through its owner's answer edit. Stale submit/confirm payloads return `409 event_date_changed` with current revision/date, never DOB. G's date hook marks affected unlocked subjects `date_review_required=true`, emits safe owner notice and invalidates their response ETags. Owner reviews/reconfirms the current revision through the existing subject edit/submit or named date-review command (§12); processing/approval locks refuse pending review. There is no reapply or loss of original queue position for reconfirmation.

Explicit lock points: ordinary registration answers lock at successful registration submission; hackathon application answers at first released decision or application close, whichever occurs first; contributor answers at first approve/decline decision or posting close, whichever occurs first. Application-close/posting-close work freezes current as-of date even if review remains pending; it does not approve the subject or clear `date_review_required`. A later approval still requires owner confirmation of that frozen revision. C adds `form_schema_version`, `application_answers`, `answer_locked_at`, `date_review_required`, `version` to `EventRoleAssignment`; its `applied` state never implies an attendee exists. Draft/owner edit is allowed before lock, withdrawal/status remain allowed afterward. Staff reopening with audited reason creates an answer revision/source snapshot, never rewrites locked history. Role withdrawal/revocation does not silently delete prior evidence or recompute it. Team/cohort lock calls lock each member's own application derivations; leaders receive completeness booleans only. Locked as-of dates stay fixed after later rescheduling, while changing/deleting vault DOB affects future drafts only. No age-based eligibility, minimum/maximum-age validation, show-if gating, reviewer filters, minors flags or guardian fields may be built.

Derivation deletion/retention follows the **typed subject's event answer retention**, not the private vault's. Owner draft deletion removes its derivations; removing a visible age question removes only its unused draft source. Submitted/locked histories follow existing event accountability retention on account erase (pseudonymize User edges as required); no unrestricted staff delete endpoint. Full event/tenant purge deletes derivations before their registration/application/role parents and retains only non-PII cleanup receipts. Global vault deletion deletes neither these independent submitted sources nor event copies of résumés. C's own-role serializer/export/erasure adapter delegates to P's subject resolver; G lists `role_assignment` FK, all subject User edges, scoped encryption/event resolver, portability remap, lifecycle graph, source guards and tombstoned retention registration explicitly. Tests use a volunteer and a mentor with **no EventRegistration** to prove submit→prefill→age/status→date revision→lock→owner export→vault DOB deletion→event purge works.

### HTTP, export and UI

Add owner-only GET `/api/v1/member/saved-details/`, PUT/DELETE `/api/v1/member/saved-details/{field_key}/`, POST `/prefill/` (mapped schema/event revision), resume asset init/complete/download/delete endpoints, and GET `/save-intents/{operation_uuid}/`. Writes use expected_version/idempotency and normal account session/claim rules; no tenant parameter grants ownership. Responses contain own plaintext only in authorized no-store HTTPS responses, never data in analytics/logs. Scoped event registration APIs add `save_choices`, base saved-detail versions and event-date revision; persist no caller-computed age. G registers all routes/fields/secret/user/object/claim/API-client/origin policies. No tenant API client can read the vault.

Member “Saved details” page in existing account settings shows each value with edit/delete, sensitive privacy labels, per-field save defaults, resume replace/download/delete and export link. Explicitly distinguish private saved details, public profile and already-submitted event answers. Inputs accessible/mobile and in the Space Works theme; no raw DOB in URL/query key/local storage. Owner data export includes vault plaintext through the account-bound encryption mapper plus own ready resume file. Add typed `AccountSavedDetailsExportJob(user,job_uuid unique,state queued/building/ready/failed/expired,object_key,sha256,size_bytes,created_at,expires_at)` using existing export/streaming/temporary-file primitives, not a fabricated tenant DataExportJob. POST `/api/v1/member/saved-details/export/` creates job, GET `/export/{job_uuid}/` gives own status, GET `/export/{job_uuid}/download/` owner-authenticated no-store archive; expire/delete after 24h, no bearer link in mail/chat. Export job/object is omitted ephemeral coordination, not canonical backup data. **Tenant exports/tenant migration never pull global vault data just because a member attended**. Tenant artifacts carry only event-submitted answer/derivation snapshots under existing PII fidelity; deployment backup owns account vault keys/objects globally. Include full field/key/User/uniqueness/object/erasure/reset dispositions and account-source guard rules before enabling.
